summary: Tested backend (17 pytest cases) and frontend e2e flows for Game Deals app. Backend 100% pass; frontend mostly working with 1 minor filter-reset bug and a code-quality issue around non-unique data-testid values on deal cards.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking the Reset button clears the filter inputs but does NOT re-fetch deals (the previous filtered result set stays on screen). Root cause: in DealsPage.js line 91-94, onReset calls setFilters() then setTimeout(() => load(0), 0). Because the memoized `load` is captured at render time, the setTimeout runs the STALE load closure (still bound to old filters). Fix: trigger reload via a useEffect on filters change, or call load with new filters explicitly, e.g. setFilters(defaults); use a `pendingApply` flag and useEffect.

data-testid values are NOT unique across cards (every card uses the same `deal-card`, `wishlist-btn`, `alert-btn`, `deal-title`). Per system guidelines, interactive elements that repeat in lists should include a unique identifier (e.g., deal-card-{dealID}, wishlist-btn-{gameID}). Makes targeted Playwright testing harder.

action_items: Fix DealsPage Reset: replace setTimeout with a useEffect that re-fetches when filters change to defaults, OR pass filters explicitly to load(filters,p).
Make deal-card / wishlist-btn / alert-btn / deal-title data-testid unique per item (suffix with dealID or gameID).
critical_code_review_comments: DealsPage.onReset has a stale-closure bug (setTimeout captures old `load`). Reset clears UI but doesn't refetch.
DealCard.js: duplicate data-testid across rendered cards breaks test selector uniqueness convention.
Backend get_alerts (server.py:365-384) iterates over alerts and makes a sequential CheapShark request per alert (N+1). For many alerts this can be slow. Consider asyncio.gather.
HomePage and DealsPage have duplicate toggleWishlist / openAlert logic — could be extracted into a shared hook (DRY).
/api/games/search route is shadowed by /api/games/{game_id} because the catch-all is declared first; calling /api/games/search will be routed to get_game with game_id='search'.
Auth cookie set with samesite='none' + secure=True requires HTTPS. Works in this preview but flag for local dev configurations.

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (1 minor reset bug, 1 testid hygiene issue)

test_credentials: Test users are dynamically registered as test+<uuid>@gamedeals.app / Test1234! (POST /api/auth/register).
seed_data_creation: Each test run creates a fresh user (TEST_ prefix not strictly used; uses unique UUID). Wishlist item with game_id='TEST_game_001' and alert with game_id='614' are created and cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_game_deals.py covers root, /deals (default+filters), /stores, full auth (register/login/me/401), wishlist CRUD, and alerts CRUD with current_price/triggered fields. All 17 pass. Frontend verified: hero/home loads with 16 cards, /deals shows 24 cards, search filter works (e.g. 'witcher' -> 15 results), theme toggle works, lang switcher AR sets dir=rtl & lang=ar, login/register persists JWT to localStorage('auth_token'), wishlist add via deal card persists to DB, alert creation persists & shows on /alerts page with WATCHING status. Outstanding bug: Reset button on DealsPage does not refetch.
rca of the issue: DealsPage Reset Bug: In /app/frontend/src/pages/DealsPage.js the onReset handler is: `() => { setFilters({...defaults}); setTimeout(() => load(0), 0); }`. React state updates are async; the setTimeout callback runs in a microtask still holding the OLD memoized `load` (with deps [filters, t]). At that moment filters has not yet re-rendered, so load() executes with the OLD filter values (including the previous search term), which means it fetches the same filtered subset rather than the unfiltered default set. The UI input value updates because setFilters re-renders, but the in-flight API call uses stale state. Repro: visit /deals, search 'witcher', Apply, then click Reset – search input clears but the 15 Witcher results remain. Fix: rely on useEffect([filters]) to re-fetch, OR explicitly pass the new filter object to a non-memoized `load(filters, page)` function.
